'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[2025 Afghanistan–Pakistan conflict]]
***[[Afghanistan]]'s [[Taliban government]] states that [[Peace process|peace talks]] with [[Pakistan]] in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]], have failed, while the [[ceasefire]] holds. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251108-taliban-govt-says-pakistan-ceasefire-to-hold-despite-talks-failing (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***[[Russia]] launches over 450 [[loitering munition|bomber drones]] and 45 missiles on [[critical infrastructure]] and residential areas across [[Ukraine]], killing at least seven people and injuring 12 others in [[Dnipro]] and [[Zaporizhzhia]], as well as damaging energy plants in the [[Oblasts of Ukraine|oblasts]] of [[Kharkiv Oblast|Kharkiv]], [[Kyiv Oblast|Kyiv]], and [[Poltava Oblast|Poltava]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce3xdg7xrv9o (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-hits-several-key-ukraine-energy-facilities-kills-three-people-2025-11-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Embargo of Russian oil during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Bulgaria]]'s [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)|parliament]] approves legal amendments giving a state-appointed manager expanded authority over [[Lukoil]]'s [[Oil refinery|refinery]] in [[Burgas]], including operational control and the power to sell [[Share (finance)|shares]], to prevent a [[Shutdown (economics)|shutdown]] when [[United States government sanctions|U.S. sanctions]] on the refinery's [[Russia]]n owner take effect. [https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-lukoil-refinery-shutdown-russia-sanctions-11eff472c05a533eb64749cd598c8187 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Six people are killed and four others are injured, including one critically, in a fire at a [[perfume]] warehouse in [[Dilovası]], [[Kocaeli Province]], [[Turkey]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0kprpy26k6o (BBC News)]
*Three people are killed and 15 others are injured by [[storm surge]]s amid rough seas off the coast of [[Tenerife]], [[Spain]]. [https://apnews.com/article/storm-surge-deaths-tenerife-canary-islands-86539457241ce2296015e1278cdb8994 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/climate-energy/three-die-heavy-seas-batter-spanish-island-tenerife-2025-11-09/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2025 G20 Johannesburg summit]], [[South Africa–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] announces that it will send no delegates to the 2025 [[G20]] [[List of G20 summits|summit]] in [[Johannesburg]], [[South Africa]], citing accusations of [[South African farm attacks|persecution]] of the [[Afrikaner]] minority. [https://apnews.com/article/trump-g20-south-africa-farmers-f2596a3a41c1736fbcc0c1c8b624caa1 (AP)]
*[[Bolivia–United States relations]]
**[[Bolivia]] and the United States announce that they will restore diplomatic relations at the ambassadorial level after 17 years. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2025/11/1311026/bolivia-and-united-states-will-reestablish-relations-ambassador-level (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mexican Police|Police]] in [[Tijuana]], [[Baja California]], [[Mexico]], arrest a man suspected of participating in the 1994 [[assassination]] of [[President of Mexico|presidential]] candidate [[Luis Donaldo Colosio Murrieta]], and take him to a maximum security prison in [[central Mexico]]. [https://apnews.com/article/new-suspect-arrested-1994-mexican-presidential-candidate-assassination-3b07ec37355a7c149dd532f825372303 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Bolivian general election]]
**[[Rodrigo Paz Pereira|Rodrigo Paz]] is sworn in as the new [[president of Bolivia]], succeeding [[Luis Arce]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/8/paz-sworn-in-as-bolivias-president-promises-capitalism-for-all (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2025 Guinean presidential election]]
**[[Guinea]]'s [[supreme court]] publishes a provisional list of nine [[List of presidents of Guinea|presidential]] candidates for the upcoming election, including [[2021 Guinean coup d'état|junta]] leader [[Mamady Doumbouya]], while excluding former [[List of prime ministers of Guinea|prime minister]] [[Lansana Kouyaté]] on procedural grounds. [https://apnews.com/article/guinea-election-president-junta-doumbouya-f886c4d739e2a157db9e980c6d683dde (AP)]
*[[2025 Tanzanian election protests]]
**[[Tanzania]]n authorities charge hundreds of people with [[treason]] over protests linked to the disputed elections, including [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] officials such as [[Chadema]] secretary-general [[John Mnyika]], while additional arrest warrants are issued for others, including [[Kawe, Kinondoni|Kawe]] [[National Assembly (Tanzania)|MP]] [[Josephat Gwajima]]. [https://apnews.com/article/tanzania-election-protests-opposition-treason-charges-aba45579e7e2d37b268f902510734399 (AP)]
*[[2026 Djiboutian presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[Djibouti]]an [[List of presidents of Djibouti|president]] [[Ismaïl Omar Guelleh]] accepts [[People's Rally for Progress|his party]]'s nomination to seek a sixth term in next year's election after [[National Assembly (Djibouti)|parliament]] lifted the [[Constitution of Djibouti|constitutional]] [[Age of candidacy|age limit]] for presidential candidates. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2025/11/08/djibouti-s-president-guelleh-announces-candidacy-for-sixth-term_6747263_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]
*[[Kenya–Uganda relations]]
**[[Uganda]]n [[President of Uganda|president]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] confirms that two [[Kenya]]n activists were detained after attending an opposition rally and accuses them of working with rival [[List of political parties in Uganda|political groups]]; both men are released to Kenyan authorities following diplomatic discussions. [https://apnews.com/article/uganda-kenyan-activists-museveni-142d6e10223d026e685f28b520d332db (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 WTA Tour]]
**[[2025 WTA Finals]]
***In [[tennis]], [[Elena Rybakina]] of [[Sport in Kazakhstan|Kazakhstan]] becomes the first Asian player to win a [[WTA Finals]] title after defeating [[Aryna Sabalenka]], 6–3, 7–6<sup>(7–0)</sup> to win the [[2025 WTA Finals – Singles|singles title]] at the [[2025 WTA Finals]]. By winning the title undefeated, Rybakina wins [[United States dollar|US$]]5.235 million in prize money, breaking the [[2024 WTA Finals|previous year]]'s record for the largest prize money earned by a female tennis player at a single event. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/c33pl2j56vgo (BBC Sports)]
